title: Best area to live in Ho Chi Minh City as a teacher (2026)
description: Ten Saigon neighbourhoods compared for teachers: median asking rents from eno.vn's Rent Index, metro access, flood-prone streets and the new ward names.
h1: Where to live in Ho Chi Minh City as an English teacher: areas, rents and commutes
intro: Choose by commute first: most language-centre teaching happens on weekday evenings and at weekends, so many teachers aim to live within 20–25 minutes of their main centre. Binh Thanh, Phu Nhuan and District 3 give central access at mid-range rents, District 2 (Thao Dien) and District 7 (Phu My Hung) suit international-school jobs nearby, and Go Vap and Tan Binh have the lowest one-bedroom rents of the ten areas compared here. These are the old district names; since July 2025 official addresses use new wards.
keyPoints: **Commute beats district label**: find out which centre or centres you will teach at before you sign a lease, then search within about 20–25 minutes of them.

**One-bedroom medians** on the [eno.vn HCMC Rent Index](/hcmc-rent-index) (10 October 2026): {{vnd:5200000}} a month in Go Vap, {{vnd:7500000}} in Binh Thanh and District 3, {{vnd:8600000}} in District 1 and {{vnd:10000000}} in District 2. Room medians run {{vnd:3800000-5300000}} across the ten areas below.
**Metro Line 1 only helps one corridor**: District 1, Binh Thanh, Thao Dien/An Phu and Thu Duc. District 3, 10, Phu Nhuan, Tan Binh, Go Vap and District 7 have no station.

**Flooding is street by street**: check the address against the city's 2025 and 2026 lists (among them Nguyen Van Huong in Thao Dien; Tran Xuan Soan, Huynh Tan Phat and Pham Huu Lau in District 7; Binh Quoi and Ung Van Khiem in Binh Thanh; Calmette in District 1; Phan Huy Ich and Pham Van Chieu in Go Vap).
**New ward names since 1 July 2025**: Thao Dien is in An Khanh ward, the Phu My Hung core in Tan Hung, and central District 1 in Sai Gon and Ben Thanh wards.
**First month**: stay short-term while you view in person, and bring cash for a deposit of 1–2 months plus the first month in advance.

sections.title: The short answer: match the area to your job

blocks.text: Most centre work is weekday evenings and weekends, often split across more than one branch. Many teachers on forums say the ride to work matters more than which district you live in, so the best area is usually the one closest to where you actually teach. Ask your employer for the address of every centre you might be scheduled at before you commit to a 12-month lease. [Working at a language centre in Ho Chi Minh City](/teach-in-vietnam/language-centre-jobs-in-ho-chi-minh-city) explains how those schedules work.

items: **Teaching at centres across the central city**: Binh Thanh, Phu Nhuan, District 3 or District 10 give central access at mid-range rents. District 1 costs a little more and can be noisy.

**Teaching at an international school in Thao Dien or Phu My Hung**: live near the campus. BIS and ISHCMC have campuses in An Khanh ward (old District 2); SSIS is in Tan Hung ward and Canadian International School in Tan My ward (old District 7). See [international school jobs in Vietnam](/teach-in-vietnam/international-school-jobs-in-vietnam).
**Keeping costs down**: Go Vap and Tan Binh have the lowest one-bedroom medians of the ten areas below, at the price of longer rides to the centre and no metro.
**Wanting to ride the metro to work**: Binh Thanh (Van Thanh, Tan Cang stations), Thao Dien/An Phu or Thu Duc, if your job is along the line.

blocks.text: A job advertised as "Ho Chi Minh City" may now be far from all of these. Under [Resolution 202/2025/QH15](https://luatvietnam.vn/hanh-chinh/nghi-quyet-202-2025-qh15-cua-quoc-hoi-ve-viec-sap-xep-don-vi-hanh-chinh-cap-tinh-402728-d1.html) the city absorbed Binh Duong and Ba Ria–Vung Tau on 1 July 2025, so Thu Dau Mot, Di An, Thuan An and Vung Tau are now part of HCMC. Those are separate commuting areas, and the Rent Index has no rows for them: check the campus address before you look for a home.

sections.title: Ho Chi Minh City neighbourhoods compared: rent, metro and flooding

blocks.text: The [eno.vn HCMC Rent Index](/hcmc-rent-index) pools asking prices from live listings on the main property sites and eno.vn, removes duplicates and publishes a median only where there are at least 10 listings. These are **asking prices, not signed leases**, so expect to settle a little lower, especially on a 12-month lease. Rows use the old district names because most listings still do. All figures below are the 10 October 2026 snapshot; the index is updated regularly, so check it for current numbers.

blocks.text: The Thu Duc row is the old Thu Duc City as a whole, which also counts listings still labelled District 2 or District 9. District 1's two-bedroom median ({{vnd:30000000}}, from only 81 listings) is pulled up by luxury stock, so don't compare all-apartment medians between District 1 and District 2 directly. For the full set of districts and housing types, see the [Rent Index](/hcmc-rent-index); to see what is on the market now, browse [rentals on eno.vn](/c/rentals).
District 1 (Sai Gon, Ben Thanh, Tan Dinh and Cau Ong Lanh wards)

The centre, with three underground metro stations and a one-bedroom median of {{vnd:8600000}} (middle half {{vnd:7300000-10900000}}). The trade-off is noise: the Bui Vien / Pham Ngu Lao backpacker strip is in Ben Thanh ward, and its weekend walking street runs late into the night. If you need sleep, don't rent on or right next to it.
District 3 (Ban Co, Xuan Hoa and Nhieu Loc wards)

Central and cheaper than District 1, with a one-bedroom median of {{vnd:7500000}} and rooms at {{vnd:4650000}}. There is no metro yet. Since 10 October 2026, Metro Line 2 station works have brought [traffic diversions](https://www.vietnamplus.vn/tp-ho-chi-minh-phan-luong-giao-thong-phuc-vu-thi-cong-ga-tao-dan-bay-hien-post1139640.vnp) making Cach Mang Thang Tam one-way near Tao Dan, so allow extra time on that axis.
Binh Thanh (Gia Dinh, Binh Thanh, Binh Loi Trung, Thanh My Tay, Binh Quoi)

The most listed central district for one-bedrooms (491 listings, median {{vnd:7500000}}), sitting between District 1 and Thao Dien. The Vinhomes Central Park / Landmark 81 area is in Thanh My Tay ward, served by Van Thanh and Tan Cang metro stations and by Vinmec Central Park hospital. Two spots to check carefully: Ung Van Khiem floods after heavy rain, and the Thanh Da / Binh Quoi peninsula (Binh Quoi ward) has flooded repeatedly at king tides, including in October and November 2025.
Phu Nhuan (Duc Nhuan, Cau Kieu and Phu Nhuan wards)

Mid-range rents (one-bedroom {{vnd:7300000}}, room {{vnd:4700000}}) close to District 3, Binh Thanh and Tan Binh. No metro station, so you rely on a motorbike, Grab, Xanh SM, Be or the bus. None of its streets is named on the city's 2025–2026 flood lists, but check the exact street.
District 2: Thao Dien and An Phu (An Khanh ward)

The highest one-bedroom median of the ten ({{vnd:10000000}}, with a wide middle half of {{vnd:7250000-18000000}}) and an all-apartment median of {{vnd:24000000}}, because larger flats dominate its listings. It makes sense if you teach at BIS, ISHCMC or another school in An Khanh ward; Thao Dien and An Phu metro stations reach Ben Thanh directly. Nguyen Van Huong is on the official tidal-flood list (a drainage upgrade is due in December 2026), and the An Phu interchange, the gateway to the area, is [targeted for full completion on 30 April 2027](https://daibieunhandan.vn/tp-ho-chi-minh-day-nhanh-trien-khai-cac-du-an-giao-thong-trong-diem-10421447.html).
District 7: Phu My Hung (Tan Hung and Tan My wards)

Cheaper per bedroom than Thao Dien: one-bedroom {{vnd:7000000}}, two-bedroom {{vnd:15000000}}. SSIS, Canadian International School, FV Hospital and a Family Medical Practice clinic are here. There is **no metro station**, whatever older blogs say, and Tran Xuan Soan, Huynh Tan Phat and Pham Huu Lau are official tidal-flood roads; tides flooded streets in former District 7 again on 27 September 2026.
Tan Binh (six wards, including Tan Son Nhat and Bay Hien)

One-bedroom {{vnd:6500000}}, room {{vnd:4200000}}, on the airport side of the city. No metro. Since 10 October 2026 Metro Line 2 works have banned through traffic from Truong Chinh at the Bay Hien junction (Truong Chinh / Cach Mang Thang Tam / Ly Thuong Kiet / Hoang Van Thu), which matters if your commute crosses it.
Go Vap (six wards, including Go Vap, An Nhon and An Hoi Tay)

The cheapest of the ten: one-bedroom {{vnd:5200000}} (middle half {{vnd:4500000-6300000}}), room {{vnd:3800000}}, two-bedroom {{vnd:9000000}}. Rides to the centre are longer and there is no metro. Phan Huy Ich and Pham Van Chieu flood after heavy rain. Even cheaper areas exist further out (District 12, Binh Tan, Tan Phu), but none of them is on Metro Line 1.
District 10 (Dien Hong, Vuon Lai and Hoa Hung wards)

Inner-city rents similar to Binh Thanh (one-bedroom {{vnd:7600000}}, room {{vnd:4700000}}), no metro, and no streets named on the city's 2025–2026 flood lists. It suits a teacher whose centres are on the west side of the inner city.
Thu Duc (Thu Duc, Hiep Binh, Linh Xuan and Tam Binh wards)

Along the far end of Metro Line 1, which runs from Ben Thanh to Suoi Tien in about 30 minutes. The old Thu Duc City row shows a one-bedroom median of {{vnd:6800000}}. The streets around Thu Duc market flood after rain; drainage works there were due in September 2026. Remember that "Thu Duc City" no longer exists and "Thu Duc ward" is now one small part of it.

sections.title: The new ward names since July 2025

blocks.text: Since 1 July 2025 Ho Chi Minh City has no districts. [Resolution 1685/NQ-UBTVQH15](https://hoatieu.vn/phap-luat/nghi-quyet-1685-nq-ubtvqh15-2025-233560) divides the merged city into 168 ward- and commune-level units, and official addresses now read "number, street, ward, Ho Chi Minh City" (the [State Bank of Vietnam's example](https://sbv.gov.vn/en/w/deutsche-bank-ag-hcmc-branch-announces-revision-of-office-address-information): 33 Le Duan Street, Sai Gon Ward). People, listings, schools and the Rent Index still use the old names, and Google Maps had only partly switched by March 2026.

blocks.text: Papers issued under the old names stay valid until they expire, and authorities may not demand reissue just because a name changed ([Resolution 190/2025/QH15, Art. 10](https://xaydungchinhsach.chinhphu.vn/quy-dinh-ve-ap-dung-su-dung-van-ban-giay-to-da-duoc-cap-ban-hanh-truoc-khi-sap-xep-bo-may-119250224120320723.htm)). Where a ward was split, check the exact street rather than guessing. When you message a landlord or driver, give both names, for example "An Khanh Ward (Thao Dien, old District 2)". Further changes, mostly turning outer communes into wards, were under discussion in 2026, but none affecting the central neighbourhoods had been decided as of October 2026.

blocks.text: On typical full-time take-home pay of about {{vnd:30500000-44300000}} a month, depending on the area, a room takes roughly 9–17%, a one-bedroom roughly 12–33% and an expat serviced flat 34–49% (eno.vn and Numbeo data; see the [English teacher salary guide](/teach-in-vietnam/english-teacher-salary-in-vietnam) for pay and the [cost of living guide](/teach-in-vietnam/cost-of-living-in-ho-chi-minh-city-for-teachers) for a full budget). Numbeo's centre figure is much higher than eno.vn's District 1 median ({{vnd:8600000}}) because it skews to expat-oriented, often serviced flats, while the Rent Index covers the whole local market.

**Electricity is the hidden cost.** The household tariff has six tiers from {{vnd:1984}} to {{vnd:3460}} a kWh before VAT, but many landlords charge a flat {{vnd:3500-5000}} a kWh. Since [Circular 60/2025/TT-BCT](https://pbgdpl.cantho.gov.vn/quy-dinh-ve-gia-ban-le-dien-sinh-hoat-1) (2 December 2025), a landlord who buys power at the household rate may not collect more in total than the EVN bill, and overcharging can bring a fine of {{vnd:20000000-30000000}} plus a refund under Decree 133/2026 ([Tuoi Tre](https://tuoitre.vn/chu-tro-thu-tien-dien-sai-se-bi-phat-nang-nguoi-thue-va-chu-nha-deu-co-noi-niem-rieng-20260503075052179.htm)). Serviced buildings metered on the business tariff are different, so ask which tariff the building pays and get the billing method in writing.

sections.title: Your first month: where to stay while you look

blocks.text: Don't rent a home from abroad. View in person, ideally after you know your centres, and stay somewhere short-term meanwhile. The checklist for your first days is in [your first weeks in Ho Chi Minh City](/teach-in-vietnam/your-first-weeks-in-ho-chi-minh-city).

items.title: Ask the employer what arrival housing they cover
items.text: Some chains include a few nights: mid-2026 job ads offered up to 6 nights' accommodation ([ILA](https://vietnamteachingjobs.com/jobs/view/for-overseas-candidates-hiring-esl-teachers-for-our-60-centres-3)) and 5 nights ([VUS](https://vietnamteachingjobs.com/jobs/view/expat-esl-teachers-wanted-for-over-65-centers-across-vietnam-join-us-now)). Housing allowances are rarely stated as an amount, so ask for the figure in writing.

items.title: Book a short stay near your main centre
items.text: A hotel, guesthouse or licensed serviced apartment for two to four weeks lets you test the commute at the hours you will actually teach. Some apartment buildings restrict short-stay guests, so check before booking a flat.

items.title: Budget the move-in cash
items.text: Expect a deposit of 1–2 months' rent plus the first month in advance. A rough first-month budget before your first salary is {{vnd:21400000-24400000}} on the room route and {{vnd:48000000-60000000}} on the one-bedroom route (our estimate from Rent Index medians and typical set-up costs, for a room at about {{vnd:4200000}} or a one-bedroom at {{vnd:8000000-10000000}}). The [deposit guide](/rental-deposit-vietnam) explains how to get it back.

items.title: View at the hours that matter
items.text: Visit in the evening to hear karaoke and traffic, and, on a street with any flood history, at peak tide (roughly 6–8am or 5–7pm). Check the motorbike ramp and basement parking.

items.title: Sign, then make sure the landlord's residence declaration is done
items.text: The landlord or building management must make your residence declaration when you move in and again after every move; ask for proof. The declaration, viewings, leases and bills are covered in [renting an apartment in Vietnam](/renting-an-apartment-vietnam-foreigner).

blocks.title: Don't sign for 12 months before you know your centres
blocks.text: Breaking a 12-month lease early usually costs you the whole deposit unless the contract has a break clause. If your schedule might move you across the city, negotiate a break clause (for example 30 days' notice after a minimum period) or start with a shorter term.

sections.title: Getting to work from each area

blocks.text: [Metro Line 1](https://vietnamnews.vn/society/1689480/historic-milestone-hcm-city-s-first-metro-line-launches-after-years-of-delay.html) runs 14 stations from Ben Thanh to Suoi Tien through District 1, Binh Thanh, Thao Dien/An Phu and Thu Duc. Single fares are {{vnd:6000-19000}} cashless or {{vnd:7000-20000}} in cash, and a monthly pass is {{vnd:300000}} ([Viet Nam News](https://vietnamnews.vn/society/1798245/hcm-city-metro-operator-targets-23-4m-revenue-this-year.html)). The 2026 timetables run it 05:00–22:00 Monday to Thursday and until 23:00 Friday to Sunday ([Tuoi Tre](https://tuoitre.vn/nld/bieu-do-tau-metro-so-1-moi-gian-cach-va-gio-van-hanh-cap-nhat-196260105154538759.htm)). Line 2, through District 3 and Tan Binh, broke ground in January 2026 and is due for completion by the end of 2030.

Everywhere else, teachers use a motorbike, ride-hailing (Grab, Xanh SM or Be) or the bus. Rides on 134 city bus routes are free until 31 December 2026 under [Resolution 09/2026/NQ-HĐND](https://luatvietnam.vn/chinh-sach/nghi-quyet-09-2026-nq-hdnd-tp-hcm-ho-tro-nguoi-dung-phuong-tien-van-tai-cong-cong-438390-d2.html); since 1 October 2026 you [tap a contactless chip bank card or a phone wallet](https://tuoitre.vn/tphcm-ngay-dau-xac-thuc-khi-di-xe-buyt-mien-phi-nguoi-dan-noi-da-qua-quen-100261001135119433.htm) to log each free trip. Fares, apps and licences are covered in [getting around Ho Chi Minh City](/teach-in-vietnam/getting-around-ho-chi-minh-city), and renting a bike in [motorbike rental in Ho Chi Minh City](/motorbike-rental-ho-chi-minh-city).

sections.title: Flooding, noise and other checks before you sign

blocks.text: HCMC has [159 flood-prone locations](https://news.tuoitre.vn/ho-chi-minh-city-steps-up-efforts-to-tackle-159-flood-prone-locations-by-2030-103260724114124165.htm), and the rainy season usually runs from May to mid or late November. The year's highest tide was forecast for 27–29 October 2026 ([Viet Nam News](https://vietnamnews.vn/environment/1800818/hcm-city-mekong-delta-face-highest-tides-of-2026.html)). Rain flooding is typically 10–30 cm and clears within about 30 minutes; tidal flooding near the river is the bigger problem for ground floors.

items: **Check the street** against the [Department of Construction's June 2026 lists](https://news.tuoitre.vn/ho-chi-minh-city-lists-most-flood-prone-streets-including-one-in-former-thao-dien-103260626100336837.htm) and the [November 2025 list of 23 tide-flooded streets](https://news.tuoitre.vn/residents-warned-of-23-frequently-flooded-streets-in-ho-chi-minh-city-103251121111338935.htm). On those streets, avoid ground-floor units and basement motorbike parking.
**Alley or main road**: housing in an alley (hẻm) is commonly quieter and cheaper than a main-road unit, but check for karaoke, construction and a workable motorbike ramp.

**Noise**: under [Decree 282/2025](https://news.tuoitre.vn/how-decree-282-applies-and-what-evidence-needed-to-curb-karaoke-noise-in-vietnam-103251223143952307.htm), karaoke and amplified noise can be acted on at any hour if it exceeds the limits (55 dBA from 21:00 to 06:00 in residential areas), but the ward needs evidence such as recordings.
**Electricity and water**: get the billing method in writing (EVN bill passed through, or a fixed rate per kWh) and note the meter readings at handover.

**Clinic nearby**: [expat-oriented hospitals and clinics](/teach-in-vietnam/healthcare-and-health-insurance-in-ho-chi-minh-city) cluster in Sai Gon, Xuan Hoa, Thanh My Tay, An Khanh, Tan Hung and Tan My wards ([Australian Government list, July 2026](https://hcmc.vietnam.embassy.gov.au/files/hchi/list_of_hospitals_jul_2026.pdf)), which matters more if you are [moving with a family](/teach-in-vietnam/moving-to-vietnam-with-family-as-a-teacher).
**Timing**: avoid moving around Tet (6 February 2027), when landlords, agents and offices shut down.

blocks.text: Rules here change often; the landlord, building management or your employer has the final word on how they apply to your lease.

faqs.q: Is Binh Thanh or District 1 better for an English teacher?
faqs.a: For most teachers Binh Thanh gives better value: one-bedroom asking rents are lower, it has two metro stations, and District 1 is one short ride away. District 1 suits you if your centres are in the core and you don't mind noise, especially near Bui Vien.

faqs.q: Is Thao Dien worth the higher rent?
faqs.a: Usually only if you work there, for example at an international school in An Khanh ward. For a centre job elsewhere, you pay the highest one-bedroom median of the ten areas in this guide and then commute back into the city.

faqs.q: Do I need to update my address on documents after the 2025 merger?
faqs.a: Not just because a ward or district name changed. Resolution 190/2025/QH15 keeps papers issued under the old names valid until they expire, and reissue with the new name is optional. Use the new ward name on new forms.

faqs.q: Is Binh Duong or Vung Tau part of Ho Chi Minh City now?
faqs.a: Yes. Since 1 July 2025 the city includes former Binh Duong and Ba Ria–Vung Tau, so a job listed as HCMC can be in Thu Dau Mot, Di An or Vung Tau. Those are separate commuting areas from central Saigon.

faqs.q: Why are Numbeo rents so much higher than eno.vn's?
faqs.a: Numbeo is crowd-sourced and skews to expat-oriented, often serviced flats. The eno.vn Rent Index is built from thousands of local-market listings. Neither is signed-lease data; use eno.vn for typical flats and Numbeo as a rough guide to serviced apartments.

faqs.q: Is it worth living far out to save money?
faqs.a: District 12, Binh Tan and Tan Phu have some of the lowest medians in the Rent Index, but none is on Metro Line 1 and rides to central centres are long. For evening and weekend shifts, the time and ride-hailing costs often eat the saving.
